My analysis of the test image at `/tmp/classify_n5q9wgnu.jpg` reveals several key diagnostic features on a soybean leaf. The leaf exhibits numerous small, angular lesions. These lesions have a distinct appearance: they are dark, reddish-brown at the center and are consistently surrounded by a prominent, water-soaked-looking yellowish-green halo. In several areas, these individual spots have begun to merge, forming larger, irregular patches of dead, brown tissue. The overall pattern gives the leaf a ragged and blighted appearance.

Comparing these visual cues to the provided knowledge base, the symptoms align most closely with Bacterial_Blight. The description for Bacterial_Blight explicitly mentions "angular lesions on leaves progressing from yellow-brown to dark reddish-brown centers with yellowish-green halos around water-soaked tissue," and "spots merging into large dead patches." This perfectly matches the presentation in the image. Other diseases like Brown_Spot or Septoria_Brown_Spot also cause spots, but the combination of angular shape, dark reddish-brown centers, and the very distinct, wide, yellowish-green halo is characteristic of Bacterial_Blight as described.
